activity.role: K'uhul Kaanul Ajaw (Divine Lord of Kaanul)
activity.notes: Yuknoom Ch'een II, also called Yuknoom the Great, ruled the Kaanul (Snake) kingdom from Calakmul during its seventh-century apogee. Current epigraphic scholarship places his accession in 636 and the end of his approximately fifty-year reign in 685 or 686. ATLAS therefore records 636–c.686, binding him to the Kaanul kingdom centered at Calakmul rather than to an undifferentiated 'Maya Civilization'.

sources.title: Simon Martin, In search of the serpent kings: From Dzibanche to Calakmul — Ancient Mesoamerica
sources.citation_text: The study identifies Yuknoom Ch'een II as the ruler who reconstituted the Kaanul kingdom at Calakmul after the 636 transition and states that his fifty-year reign ended in either 685 or 686.

sources.title: The Metropolitan Museum of Art — A Maya Game of Thrones and Artistic Innovation in Golden Kingdoms
sources.citation_text: The Met dates Yuknoom Ch'een II's reign to AD 636–686 and describes his network of vassal rulers and Calakmul's political ascendancy under his rule.

review_context.correction_note: Register as ruler of the Kaanul/Snake kingdom centered at Calakmul, not as a generic ruler of all Maya civilization.
